svg.title: Batch-one decode sits far below the H100's compute-bound threshold; long or batched prefill can reach it.
svg.desc: On an H100 SXM running dense BF16 or FP16 Tensor Core math (989 TFLOPS at 3.35 TB/s), the critical intensity is about 295 FLOPs per byte. Batch-one decode runs at roughly 1 FLOP per byte, about 295x below that threshold, so it stays memory-bound. Long or sufficiently batched prefill reuses weights across large matrix multiplications and can reach the compute-bound region; short prefills may still be limited by memory traffic or kernel-launch overhead.

text.font-family: Space Grotesk, IBM Plex Sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: Decode and prefill sit on opposite sides of one threshold
